I am originally from Bangladesh, and my love of stories, learning, and helping people find exactly the right resource has steadily shaped my long-term direction. One of my clearest personal memories is watching a younger family member proudly use their very first library card at an event I helped organise, before asking me to recommend “a book with adventure and facts.” That moment brought together everything that draws me to this profession: the chance to make knowledge feel welcoming and accessible to everyone, from first-time readers to lifelong researchers. Through my Doctorate at a university not listed in the major global rankings, I developed advanced research habits and completed 3 projects with tangible outcomes, experiences that strengthened my understanding of how information can be organised, interpreted, and shared in ways that are genuinely useful.

In addition, I have always enjoyed exploring how better systems can make discovery easier. In one recent setting, I needed to use a new digital tool for organising and retrieving materials; within a few weeks I was using it confidently in my own work, and soon afterwards I was showing colleagues how to get started with the same system. On another occasion, our team kept losing time to a recurring issue in how requests were tracked, so I put together a practical workaround that simplified the process and reduced the delays we were dealing with day to day. Outside of formal responsibilities, colleagues sometimes come to me with questions in my own area, and I value those conversations because they often lead to clearer answers and better support for users. Although my interest began with books and learning, these experiences confirmed how much I enjoy connecting people with information efficiently and thoughtfully. Consequently, I am eager to contribute this combination of research experience, practical organisation, and public-facing purpose in a Librarian role.

reference_text:
Between a well-chosen story and a well-timed piece of information, libraries offer something quietly powerful: the chance for people to feel both informed and welcomed. That is what drew me to librarianship. A love of stories, learning, and helping people find exactly the right information inspired me to become a librarian, where curiosity and community service come together every day. I am especially motivated by creating welcoming spaces that make knowledge feel accessible to everyone. Originally from the Netherlands, I bring a strong academic foundation to this path, having completed a Doctorate at a university ranked in the global top 500. Across my academic and professional work, I have completed 5 projects with tangible outcomes, experiences that strengthened my approach to research, organisation, and clear communication. One area that particularly held my attention was the challenge of making complex information easier to navigate, which led me to explore how classification, discovery tools, and reader support can shape a person’s confidence in finding answers.

Over time, I have built my practice steadily and practically. When I first began using a new digital cataloguing and information-management tool, I was not immediately fluent with it; after more than a year of regular use, testing features in day-to-day tasks, and returning to guidance notes, I became comfortable enough to use it confidently in routine work. In one team setting, a recurring issue with duplicated resource records kept slowing everyone down, so I introduced a simple shared checking step before entries were finalised, which reduced repeated corrections and helped the workflow move more smoothly. I also value working closely with colleagues: when teammates have asked how I located a difficult source or organised a search trail, I have talked them through my process so they could use it in their own work.

That same sense of connection is what keeps this profession personal for me. One of my favourite memories was watching a younger family member beam with pride after I helped them get their very first library card during a family visit to my branch. Seeing my work spark their excitement about books made my career feel deeply personal as well as professional. Looking ahead, I am eager to contribute as a Librarian by helping patrons feel supported and empowered through thoughtful research support, reader’s advisory, and well-organised access to knowledge.
